content: A simulated pregnancy refers to a deliberate effort to create the false appearance of being pregnant. It is important to distinguish this from a condition known as false pregnancy (pseudocyesis), in which a woman genuinely believes she is pregnant despite the absence of an actual pregnancy. In some cases, women may choose to use artificially supplied hormones to induce physiological changes in their bodies that mimic the effects of pregnancy. This approach represents the most authentic form of simulated pregnancy currently known, as it causes the body to undergo changes similar to those experienced during a real pregnancy. For women who wish to appear pregnant for social or psychological reasons, there are alternative methods available, such as wearing specially designed body suits or similar devices beneath their clothing to create the visual impression of pregnancy.
